extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and requirements governing how postsecondary institutions must structure and carry out Title IX sex-based harassment grievance procedures, including rules on questioning, evidence access and weighing, live hearings or alternatives, and required training and impartiality safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of questions about complainant's sexual interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about the complainant's sexual interests are always excluded as impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarifies that questions about the complainant's sexual interests would always be excluded as impermissible under the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on questions about complainant's prior sexual conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about the complainant's prior sexual conduct are excluded as impermissible unless offered to prove that someone other than the respondent committed the alleged conduct or are evidence about specific incidents of the complainant's prior sexual conduct with the respondent offered to prove consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.45(b)(7)(iii). Whether other questions about a party's prior sexual conduct are harassing is a fact-specific determination depending on content, manner, and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unclear or harassing questions to parties and witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must not permit questions that are unclear or harassing of the party or witness being questioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ban on unclear or harassing questions applies to both parties and witnesses; evaluation depends on content, manner, and purpose. Language revised in §106.46(f)(3) clarifies this application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions may adopt and apply reasonable decorum rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution may 'adopt and apply other reasonable rules regarding decorum.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation text was revised to state 'adopt and apply' instead of 'impose' to provide additional clarity about institutional ability to set and enforce decorum rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker must explain exclusions of proposed questions
rubrics_metrics.description: A decisionmaker must explain any decision to exclude a proposed question as impermissible, as well as for relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to §106.46(f)(3) require explanation when questions are excluded and provide transparency about exclusion grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to clarify or revise unclear/harassing questions
rubrics_metrics.description: A party must have the opportunity to clarify or revise a question that the decisionmaker has determined is unclear or harassing, and the question must be asked if sufficiently clarified or revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.46(f)(3) was revised to require this opportunity so parties can attempt to salvage questions found unclear or harassing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker discretion in weighing statements after refusal to answer
rubrics_metrics.description: A decisionmaker may determine the weight to be given, if any, to a statement made by a party or witness who refuses to respond to questions deemed relevant and not impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.46(f)(4) provides flexibility based on the totality of the circumstances, addressing concerns that a rigid rule would be difficult to implement or manipulable by parties. It permits giving less weight but does not require exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of 'questions related to credibility' limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference to 'questions related to credibility' was removed; §106.46(f)(4) now applies to questions in general and not just those related to credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department removed that phrasing because it was confusing and context-dependent; decisionmaker now evaluates refusals to answer across all relevant, non-impermissible questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of reasons for refusal when assessing weight
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of weighing evidence, a decisionmaker may take into account reasons why a party or witness refused to answer questions (e.g., intentional avoidance vs. inability to recall).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include intentionally refusing to prevent testing of earlier statements or answering nearly all relevant questions and giving reasonable justification for skipping a small number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to witnesses as well as parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The provision regarding refusal to respond and weighing of statements applies to witnesses in the same manner as it applies to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department revised §106.46(f)(4) to make clear it applies equally to witnesses and parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on drawing inferences solely from refusal to answer
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient is restricted from drawing inferences about whether sex-based harassment occurred based solely on a party's or witness's refusal to respond to questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to remove 'solely'—decisionmakers may not base a finding solely on refusal; they may, however, consider refusal among other evidence (citing Baxter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'statements' excludes non-assertive evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Statements' applies to any statement of a party or witness and 'would not include evidence (such as videos) that do not constitute a person's intent to make factual assertions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that non-assertive artifacts are not 'statements' for purposes of §106.46(f)(4). See 85 FR 30349.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmakers must evaluate relevant evidence for persuasiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers are required to evaluate all relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence for its persuasiveness when determining whether sex-based harassment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement in §106.45(h)(1) encompasses weighing credibility and the totality of evidence; §106.46(f)(4) is interpreted in light of that obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearings optional; alternative live-questioning process required
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institutions are permitted, but not required, to hold live hearings; if they do not use live hearings they must provide another live-questioning process enabling decisionmakers to assess credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department maintains that case law does not require live hearings in all cases as long as institutions provide a meaningful alternative live-questioning process (see July 2022 NPRM discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearings may be conducted with parties physically separate
rubrics_metrics.description: If a postsecondary institution chooses to use a live hearing, it may conduct the live hearing with the parties physically present in separate locations, including virtually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses concerns about in-person interaction and trauma; allows virtual or physically separate locations to reduce contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal access to relevant evidence and investigative reports
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide each party with an equal opportunity to access the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence or an accurate description of such evidence, and a reasonable opportunity to respond; for student-party cases institutions must provide equal opportunity to access either the evidence or the same written investigative report summarizing the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a description is provided, the recipient must provide access to the evidence upon request. §106.45(f)(4) and §106.46(e)(6)(i) set out these requirements to promote transparency regardless of hearing format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and conflict-of-interest/bias prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and other persons implementing grievance procedures must receive training on topics including how to serve impartially, avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest and bias, the meaning/application of 'relevant', and impermissible evidence; designated persons are prohibited from having a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations require training (§106.8(d)) and prohibit conflicts/bias (§106.45(b)(2)). Training applies regardless of whether live hearings are used and supports fair, transparent procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional discretion to structure grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institutions have latitude to determine how to structure grievance procedures (including whether to use live hearings) to ensure they are equitable while accommodating their administrative structure, educational community, and applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department declines to mandate live hearings in particular circumstances and emphasizes that applicable case law or other law may nonetheless require specific approaches; recipients must, however, comply with final regulations and nondiscrimination requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient obligation to carry out grievance procedures nondiscriminatorily and equitably
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must carry out grievance procedures in a nondiscriminatory manner (§106.31) and treat complainants and respondents equitably (§106.45(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone who believes a recipient's treatment constitutes sex discrimination may file a complaint with OCR; these obligations apply regardless of the institution's resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live-questioning process mechanics when no live hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient chooses not to use a live hearing, §106.46(f)(1)(i) allows either the investigator or the decisionmaker to ask questions of parties and witnesses during individual meetings; if the investigator asks questions, the decisionmaker relies on the investigator's assessment of credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the ability to probe credibility through individual questioning even when a live hearing does not occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility regarding appeals and new evidence/hearing format
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require live hearings during appeals if new evidence is presented; institutions are not precluded from providing a live hearing on appeal if law or institutional discretion requires it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in final regulations precludes institutions from providing live hearings during appeals when applicable case law or institutional policy calls for it.
